item.title: “Monks, the arising, the continuation, the production, the manifestation of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging…
item.description:
“Monks, the arising, the continuation, the production, the manifestation of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. The arising … of the ear … of the nose … of the tongue … of the body … of the mind is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. The cessation, the stilling, the ending of the eye is the cessation of suffering, the stilling of disease, the ending of aging and death. The cessation … of the ear … of the nose … of the tongue … of the body … of the mind is the cessation of suffering, the stilling of disease, the ending of aging and death.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 26.1

item.title: “And, Carpenter, where are these unwholesome thoughts abandoned without remainder? Their abandoning has also been taught. Here, Carpenter, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded…
item.description:
“And, Carpenter, where are these unwholesome thoughts abandoned without remainder? Their abandoning has also been taught. Here, Carpenter, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. Here, those unwholesome thoughts are abandoned without remainder.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 78 – Samaṇamuṇḍikasutta

item.title: “Why laughter, why joy, When the world is always burning? Shrouded in darkness, Why do you not seek a light?” “Behold this painted image, This…
item.description:
“Why laughter, why joy,
When the world is always burning?
Shrouded in darkness,
Why do you not seek a light?”

“Behold this painted image,
This heap of wounds,
Diseased, full of many thoughts,
Of nothing stable or lasting.”

“This form is worn out,
A nest of diseases, fragile;
This putrid mass breaks apart —
Death is the end of life.”

“Like a gourd in autumn,
Abandoned and cast away,
Seeing these bleached bones,
What pleasure can there be?”

From: Dhammapada 146-156

item.title: “For a person who lives heedlessly, Craving grows like a creeping vine. He leaps from life to life, Like a monkey seeking fruit in the…
item.description:
“For a person who lives heedlessly,
Craving grows like a creeping vine.
He leaps from life to life,
Like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest.”

“Whoever in this world is overcome by this wretched clinging,
His sorrows increase like well-watered birana grass.”

“Whoever in this world overcomes this wretched clinging,
Sorrows fall away from him like water drops from a lotus.”

From: Dhammapada 334-359

item.title: - “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.…
item.description:
- “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. This very cause, this very reason, Venerable Bharadvāja, is why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, do not indulge in sensual pleasures and live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully. I too, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body unguarded, speech unguarded, mind unguarded, mindfulness unestablished, sense faculties unrestrained — then lust overcomes me. But, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body guarded, speech guarded, mind guarded, mindfulness established, sense faculties restrained — then lust does not overcome me.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.127

item.title: Elder Rāhula: Blinded by sensual desires, Covered by the net of wrong views, Craving acts as a veil, Covering, hiding completely. Bound by heedlessness, Like…
item.description:
Elder Rāhula:

Blinded by sensual desires,
Covered by the net of wrong views,
Craving acts as a veil,
Covering, hiding completely.
Bound by heedlessness,
Like a fish caught in a net.

I have overcome those sensual desires,
Cut Māra’s bondage.
Having pulled out the root of craving,
I am cooled, at peace.

From: Theragāthā 4.8

item.title: “Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Renunciation thought, non-ill-will thought, harmlessness thought. These, Carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.”
item.description:
“Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Renunciation thought, non-ill-will thought, harmlessness thought. These, Carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 78 – Samaṇamuṇḍikasutta

item.title: “Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because of that, delight arises. Migajāla, I say that with the arising of delight, suffering arises. Sounds … Odors … Tastes … Touches … Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk delights in them, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because of that, delight arises. Migajāla, I say that with the arising of delight, suffering arises.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.64

item.title: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick —…
item.description:
“Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would burn for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and no one occasionally pours in oil or adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being without its own fuel, with no further fuel added, not being nourished, would be extinguished. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are fetters — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.54
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing;…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors … tastes … touches cognizable by the body — desirable … enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. To abandon these five strands of sensual pleasure, monks, the four foundations of mindfulness should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.65
